key_insight: Visual language models match or exceed humans on high-level object recognition but show widespread deficits on standardized low- and mid-level neuropsychological vision tests, revealing a fundamental mismatch with human visual abilities.
problem_solved: Evaluates whether current VLMs possess foundational visual processing skills (low- and mid-level vision) beyond object recognition, exposing overlooked weaknesses that standard benchmarks miss.
method: Applied a battery of standardized neuropsychological visual tests spanning low-, mid-, and high-level tasks to multiple state-of-the-art VLMs.
Compared model performance to human normative data and analyzed error patterns to localize deficits (e.g., contrast, spatial frequency, contour integration).
Reported systematic failures in low-/mid-level tasks despite strong performance on high-level object recognition benchmarks.
impact: Shows that high-level benchmarks can mask critical low-level failures; practitioners should adopt multi-scale, neuropsychology-inspired evaluations to improve robustness, interpretability, and real-world reliability of vision systems.
visual_elements: Bar chart: human vs VLM performance grouped by visual level (low, mid, high)
Example stimulus panel: sample images for each neuropsych test with model responses and human norms
Heatmap or confusion matrix: error patterns across tests highlighting systematic deficits
Schematic timeline: mapping neuropsychological tests to visual processing stages (low → mid → high)
paper_title: Visual language models show widespread visual deficits on neuropsychological tests
